title: The compound eye of Orgyia antiqua (Lepidoptera: Lymantriidae): Sexual dimorphism and light/dark adaptational changes
why: Orgyia antiqua: the abstract describes the superposition compound eyes of the winged male and the wingless female by light and electron microscopy (eye size, regularity of the ommatidial array, width of the clear zone, tracheal tapetum), so it may give ommatidial counts, facet diameters or an interommatidial angle from which acuity (acuity_cpd) can be worked out for a species of the genus. The stored abstract holds no numbers. Top hit for the harvest query "Orgyia vision" and for the web search "Orgyia visual acuity"; not opened.

title: Eyes of male and female Orgyia antiqua (Lepidoptera; Lymantriidae) react differently to an exposure with UV-A
why: Orgyia antiqua: a microscopy-journal study of male and female eyes after UV-A exposure; the harvest stored no abstract, so it may describe the eye's ommatidia with counts or facet sizes that bear on acuity (acuity_cpd), or it may report only damage. Second paper on the eyes of the same species as the 2007 European Journal of Entomology study; not opened.
